title: Renewal scorecard: measurements and sample KPI table
body:
Purpose:
This working doc defines the canonical metric calculations we use in customer QBRs and renewal scorecards. The intent is to standardize definitions across CS, Solutions, and SRE so that renewal conversations reference identical numbers. This is a draft — expect iteration after team review and one validation pass against production telemetry (see linked jira ticket CS-427).

Metric definitions (summary):
- Request latency: measured at the request level from gateway receive timestamp to final byte sent. Reported percentiles: p50, p90, p95, p99. Window: rolling 30d for trend, 7d for recent, 1d for incident review. Exclude synthetic health checks and internal infra probes.
  - Example: p90 generation latency = time from POST /v1/generate receipt to completion of last chunk. For streaming flows, use end-of-stream timestamp.
- Uptime / availability: percent of successful responses (2xx) over total requests, measured hourly and aggregated to daily rolling windows. SLA availability = 99.95% monthly for dedicated customers; for hosted tiers we report both regional and global aggregates. Exclude scheduled maintenance windows recorded in maintenance calendar.
- Cost per effective token: blended cost metric that maps infrastructure cost and model-selection overhead to customer usage. Calculated as: (inference infra cost allocated to customer in window + model-routing surcharge) / effective_generated_tokens. Effective_generated_tokens counts only final tokens emitted to clients (not internal preloads). Show separate columns for embedding tokens vs generation tokens because unit economics differ.
- Cache hit rate: fraction of requests served from prefix/KV cache (i.e., no model execution) over eligible requests. Eligibility rules: only requests that match cacheable pattern (in the request metadata flag cacheable=true and not streaming with ephemeral contexts). We report both raw hit rate and normalized hit rate (hits / eligible_requests where eligible_requests excludes requests blocked by policy).

Measurement details and conventions:
- Timezones: all metrics use UTC and ISO timestamps.
- Percentiles: compute from raw request latency samples using interpolation for sparse buckets. For small customers (<100 requests/day) include a note about sample size and prefer averages + medians.
- Attribution: metrics in the QBR are attributed to the customer's API key(s) used in the billing window. If a customer has mixed dedicated and hosted routes, show split rows and a combined aggregated row.
- Sampling: for very high-volume customers we use 1/10k sampling for full trace capture but compute percentiles from unsampled gateway histograms (not from sampled traces).

KPI table (sample rows — paste into slide or spreadsheet):
"Customer,Period,Requests,Eligible cache requests,Cache hits,Cache hit rate (raw),Cache hit rate (normalized),p50 latency (ms),p90 latency (ms),p99 latency (ms),Uptime (%),Cost per gen token ($),Cost per embed token ($),Notes"
"AcmeCorp,2026-01,1,245,90,0.0367,0.367,120,310,820,99.984,0.00034,0.00012,dedicated: high burst, prefix cache warmed"
"BetaRetail,2026-01,82,4000,3400,0.85,0.85,45,112,305,99.992,0.00022,0.00008,heavy prompt reuse, recommend batching tweaks"
"FinServeX,2026-01,15000,14000,4200,0.28,0.3,220,650,1400,99.91,0.0012,0.00018,split hosted+dedicated, observed backfill during deploy"

Alerting thresholds (starter):
- Latency: p90 > baseline_p90 * 1.5 for >30m -> severity 2. Baseline_p90 derived from last 30d median p90.
- Uptime: rolling 1h availability < 99.5% -> severity 1.
- Cost per token: month-over-month increase >30% without corresponding model switch note -> pager to CS-ENG on-call.
- Cache hit rate: drop in normalized hit rate >20% from prior 7d -> investigate prompt drift / key mismatch.

How CS should use this doc in QBRs:
- Import the KPI table CSV above into the QBR deck, add a short interpretation for each metric (trend, immediate risk, action items).
- For renewals, include cost per effective token and projected 12mo unit cost under two scenarios: (1) current config, (2) with recommended optimizations (batching + quantization + cache warmers).
- Link to engineering tickets for any operational items; use the linked github/pr for rollout notes.

Open questions / TODOs (for next revision):
- Standardize formula for allocating infra cost across multi-tenant hosts (currently handled by infra-finance; need a reproducible notebook).
- Decide canonical minimum sample size for reporting p99 on small customers.
- Add examples for streaming vs chunked-generation accounting.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-04 Elena Martinez created initial draft.
- 2026-02-20 Marco Li updated cache eligibility rules and added sample KPI rows.

Notes and references:
- See Confluence: QBR Templates and the CS playbook (linked).
- Related tickets: CS-427 (validate metrics), ENG-991 (cache telemetry schema), FIN-210 (cost allocation spreadsheet).
